slides.title: Places and Community
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 3 English, Unit 4: Places and Community. In this unit you will explore the places in your community and the people who help you there. You will learn to name places like the hospital, the market, the court, the college and the garden, and to talk about helpers like the doctor, the officer and the sailor. You will describe places using words like quiet and busy, give clear instructions, ask questions with do and does, and explain your ideas with the word “because”. By the end, you will be ready to write your own report about a place in your community — just like Amal does in this unit's story. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Name places in your community and the people who work there.
Describe a place using adjectives and opposites, like quiet and busy.
Give simple instructions using imperatives (“Exit the court quietly.”).
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to name places in your community and the people who work there. You will also describe a place using adjectives and opposites, like quiet and busy. You will also give simple instructions using imperatives (“Exit the court quietly.”) Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Words to learn
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: noise, choice, enjoy, annoy, job, beneath. Listen to each word, look at what it means, and try to use it when you talk and write.

slides.title: Read and think
bullets: Point to the words that show it
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes Our Community and A Poem: “Places I Know”. Read slowly, look at the pictures, and find the big idea in each text. When you answer a question, point to the words that show it.

slides.title: Imperatives (Giving Instructions)

Try it in your own sentences
slides.narration: The first language focus is Imperatives (Giving Instructions). An imperative is a special way to use a verb to give a command or an instruction. It tells someone to do something. We need imperatives to give clear directions, like “Exit the court quietly” or “Go to the hospital if you are sick.” Look at the examples, then try the pattern in your own sentences.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Say it, write it, make it better
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1 — My Community. Say your ideas clearly and listen to your partner. In writing, you will draw, trace, copy or write, then check your work with a grown-up or the AI tutor.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the words, then the reading and the questions, then the grammar, speaking and writing. Ask the AI tutor for help any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
